header.running_head: Exercising Patience upon Misfortunes in General

blocks.text: Umar (RA) say, 'O Abu Ahmad! Move away from the bier so the people will not hurt you.' However, Abu Ahmad (RA) replied, 'O Umar! It is from her that I received every good. This (carrying her bier) cools the heat of the grief I am feeling.' 'Then hold on tight,' Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'Hold on tight.'"[^1]
The Patience of the Muslims upon the death of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Ahnaf bin Qais (RA) says, "I once heard Hadhrat Umar (RA) say, 'The Quraysh are leaders and when any of them enter a door, an entire group of people enter with them.' I however did not fully understand what he meant until he was stabbed. On his deathbed, he instructed Suhayb (RA) to lead the salaah for three days and also gave instructions for food to be served to the people until his successor was appointed. When the people returned from the funeral, the food was served and the tablecloths laid out. However, because of their grief, the people refrained from eating. Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) then said, 'O people! We ate and drank after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ and we also ate and drank after the demise of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Now it is also necessary for us to eat this food." He then stretched out his hand and ate. The people followed suit. I then understood what Hadhrat Umar (RA) said about the Quraysh being leaders."[^2]
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Advise People to Exercise Patience upon the Deaths of Close Relatives

Hadhrat Abu Uyaynah (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) consoled a person, he said, "There is no calamity when there is patience and no benefit when there is impatience. What precedes death is simple while that which follows it is difficult. If you think of the loss of Rasulullaah ﷺ, your tragedy will seem light and Allaah will inflate your reward."[^3]

Hadhrat Sufyaan reports that when consoling Hadhrat Ash'ath bin Qais (RA) upon the death of his son, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "It is the right of your family relationship that you should grieve but if you exercise patience, Allaah shall replace the loss of your son. If you are patient, fate will take its course and you will be rewarded. However, if you are irritated, fate will still take its course and you will be sinful."[^4]
